meta.definition: Implied volatility is the yearly swing the option market is paying for, read from NIFTY options about 30 days out; India VIX measures the same thing with NSE's own formula, so the two lines should travel together. Skew is how much more a 5% downside put costs than an at-the-money option, in volatility points: it rises when investors pay up for crash insurance. The put-call ratio divides open put contracts by open call contracts across all expiries; high readings mean heavy hedging.
meta.technical: Black-76 on NSE F&O bhavcopy settle prices, strikes with at least 5 traded contracts, 30-day constant maturity by variance-time interpolation between the two nearest expiries; skew05 = implied vol of the 95% put minus at-the-money; put-call ratios on open interest and traded contracts, all expiries; VIX close from Yahoo ^INDIAVIX.
